With hierarchically generated data the spectrum falls with depth in the tree, so the schedule is coarse to fine. It is not a claim about nonlinear networks, about correlated inputs, or about learning that starts from prior knowledge. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-187](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-187.md) | In a deep linear network trained by gradient descent, depth slows learning through the initial end-to-end strength of each mode: from strength of order one the number of iterations stays bounded as depth grows, once the step size falls with depth as stability requires, while from small strength ε the plateau lengthens from ln(1/ε) with one hidden layer towards 1/ε at great depth | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2014), [LIT-864](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-864.md), Eqs. 13–17 and Appendix B: exact for decoupled initial weights and whitened inputs, with the step size bounded by the Hessian at the optimum, and supported on MNIST from decoupled starts up to 100 layers. It does not show that random orthogonal initialisation is such a start. The paper's account of that, isometry of the product of layers, is argued and simulated, not derived. It says nothing about nonlinear networks' learning time, and it is not advice on how to initialise. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-195](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-195.md) | On data generated by a random hierarchical grammar, deep networks that learn features need a number of examples polynomial in the input dimension, about n_c m^L, which is where the class statistics of input patches, equal for interchangeable patches, rise above sampling noise and where hidden layers become invariant to swapping them; shallow and fixed-kernel learners need an exponential number, and so do deep ones when those statistics are removed | Cagnetta, Petrini, Tomasini, Favero and Wyart (2023), [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md): measured for depth-(L + 1) CNNs and deep fully connected networks on the Random Hierarchy Model with s = 2 and L ≤ 4, with a large-v scaling argument for the correlation threshold and an exact one-step-gradient model of a two-layer network on one patch. The law n_c m^L is fitted, not proved for trained deep networks, and in this model the correlation threshold and the grammar's size are the same expression, so the data cannot say which of the two sets it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-200](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-200.md) | On sparse hierarchical data, deep networks become insensitive to swapping synonymous parts and to small displacements of informative features at the training-set size at which they learn the task | Tomasini and Wyart (2024), [LIT-880](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-880.md): measured for locally connected, convolutional and fully connected networks on the Sparse Random Hierarchy Model with s ≤ 3 and L ≤ 3, with thresholds for the two sensitivities tuned per setting; the sample size is about (s0 + 1)^L n_c m^L times s^(L/2) without weight sharing, with a one-step argument for the (s0 + 1)^L, and about (s0 + 1)^2 n_c m^L with it, unexplained. Both invariances keep the parent's label statistics by construction, so the model shows that trained networks do the grouping, not that the invariances could not separate, and the extension to images is an analogy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-201](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-201.md) | In next-token prediction on hierarchically generated sequences, the correlation between two tokens falls by about a factor m per level of their common ancestor, so a training set of P sequences resolves correlations only out to a distance t*(P) at which they meet sampling noise; learners come to represent the hidden symbols up to that depth, giving loss steps at about v m^(2ℓ−1) examples, and on character-level text the context at which the loss saturates grows as P^(1/(2β)) with β the measured correlation decay | Cagnetta and Wyart (2024), [LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md), extending [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md) from labels to masked tokens: the correlation plateaus and the noise floor are derived for the Random Hierarchy Model in the large-v, large-m limit; the loss steps and the representation probes are measured in small transformers and CNNs; the link between them is argued, not proved; and the real-text evidence, from two character-level corpora, tests the effective context window, not the hierarchy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-204](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-204.md) | In data-limited next-token prediction, the test loss falls as P^(−γ/(2β)), where β is the decay with lag of the strongest token–token covariance and γ the decay of next-token conditional entropy with context length, because P tokens resolve correlations only out to a horizon n*(P) ~ P^(1/(2β)) and the loss is the entropy at that horizon, provided the learner uses the tokens inside the horizon faster than the horizon grows | Cagnetta, Raventós, Ganguli and Wyart (2026), [LIT-888](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-888.md), building on [LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md)'s effective context window. The exponent is derived from assumed scaling forms for the conditional entropy and for each lag's learning curve, not proved; it is matched on two corpora, TinyStories and WikiText-103, with transformers up to about 10^8 tokens and horizons of tens of tokens, with γ estimated from trained models' own n-gram losses. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-206](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-206.md) v2 | For networks of smooth units without biases, one hidden layer needs exactly ∏(rᵢ+1) neurons to match the monomial x₁^r₁⋯xₙ^rₙ's Taylor polynomial at the origin, and a deep network O(Σ log rᵢ), with the upper bounds holding for uniform approximation too, so the cost of flattening a polynomial grows exponentially with its degree in distinct variables and not with the number of inputs: products of many inputs separate depths, bounded-degree polynomials do not | Rolnick and Tegmark (2017), [LIT-890](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-890.md), Theorems 4.1 to 4.3, extending Lin, Tegmark and Rolnick's 2ⁿ for a product ([LIT-887](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-887.md)). Proved for Taylor matching at the origin with bias-free units; the uniform version's lower bound rests on an unproved step. The flip side, that a polynomial of degree d with c monomials costs one layer at most c·2ᵈ however many inputs it has, is the edge: the separation does not reach the low-order polynomials [LIT-887](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-887.md) calls natural. | Active |
| [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md) | A converged network trained with SGD is not at a point and does not sample its training loss: under a quadratic approximation it samples a Gibbs distribution on a modified loss, isotropic in the Hessian's column space, with probability currents that keep it oscillating, so its speed and spread are set by the learning rate, momentum and batch size | Kunin et al. (2021), [LIT-1011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1011.md), read in [NOTE-711](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-711.md). Modelled as an underdamped Langevin equation with noise covariance proportional to the Hessian, SGD at the end of training converges to a nonequilibrium stationary state: Gibbs on a modified loss whose curvature undoes the Hessian's anisotropy, with inverse temperature S(1 − β²), in broken detailed balance. A ResNet-18 on ImageNet explores isotropically in a plane where the loss is anisotropic, oscillates at Hessian-dependent rates, and moves at the predicted speed across a hyperparameter sweep. For the learned-structure line, a trained solution is in part a property of the regime that trained it. Proposed: the deep-learning evidence is one network, under assumptions the paper concedes are strained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-210](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-210.md) v2 | Continuous parameter symmetries stretch a network's minima into connected manifolds along which the loss is flat, and give gradient flow conserved quantities that fix where on such a manifold training ends; finite steps, gradient noise and weight decay break them, so the position along a symmetry orbit is set by initialization and optimizer, not by the loss | Zhao, Walters & Yu (2025), [LIT-970](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-970.md), read in [NOTE-712](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-712.md): a survey, so the dynamical results are secondhand. Continuous parameter-space symmetries (GL, scaling, orthogonal, translation) make minima positive-dimensional and connected, which is one source of mode connectivity. Under gradient flow each gives a conserved quantity, such as layer imbalance, that is fixed by initialization and locates the endpoint on the manifold. Under SGD these are not conserved. Read first-hand (Neural Mechanics; Ziyin et al.), weight decay drives the conserved quantities toward zero, and minibatch noise drives a rescaling symmetry's toward the point where the layers' gradient noise balances. The survey had reported this as imbalance decaying with large learning rates, and a stationary distribution biased toward balanced solutions that a Langevin model does not predict. This is the null-space half that [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md)'s limiting dynamics leave out. Proposed: one survey, with the SGD results unread here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md) | Along a rescaling symmetry, minibatch noise drives SGD to the point where the gradient noise of the two parameter groups balances, at a rate set by learning rate over batch size, so at stationarity SGD neither stays where gradient flow would leave it nor diffuses as isotropic noise would, and differs from gradient descent by a finite amount however small the noise | Ziyin, Li & Ueda ([LIT-1012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1012.md), read in [NOTE-714](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-714.md)), with the gradient flow conservation law and the Itô term from Neural Mechanics ([LIT-1013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1013.md)). If ℓ(u, w) = ℓ(λu, w/λ) for every sample, then under the SDE model of SGD d(‖u‖² − ‖w‖²)/dt = −T(uᵀC₁u − wᵀC₂w), with T = η/S. The noise has no component along the symmetry, but its dependence on the parameters produces a deterministic drift through Itô's lemma. The drift points to the noise-balanced point, and weight decay adds to its rate. In a diagonal linear network the stationary distribution follows exactly: it is non-ergodic, has a memory of initialization, and collapses to zero above a critical temperature. Proposed: the theorem's proof was not checked here, and the tests are small synthetic networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-212.md) | In a two-layer linear network trained by gradient flow, the relative scale of the two layers, which gradient flow conserves, sets the learning regime: balanced layers learn in sigmoidal stages and both build task-specific representations, while strongly unbalanced layers learn exponentially with a static kernel and leave the larger layer task-agnostic | Dominé et al. (2025), [LIT-943](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-943.md), read in [NOTE-715](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-715.md). With whitened inputs and a λ-balanced start, W₂ᵀW₂ − W₁W₁ᵀ = λI, the full gradient flow is solved exactly. λ is conserved and sets the regime. As λ → 0, singular values are learned in sigmoidal stages, as in Saxe et al., and both layers become task-specific. As \|λ\| → ∞, learning is exponential, the NTK is static, and the larger layer stays near the identity while the smaller carries the task at scale ∝ 1/\|λ\|. The paper analyses gradient flow only. Under SGD the conserved quantity drifts ([THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md)), which [QUESTION-081](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-081.md) takes up. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-213](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-213.md) | Every mirror symmetry of a network's loss makes its symmetric subspace absorbing for gradient-based training, and weight decay above a threshold or strong gradient noise makes that subspace favoured, so rescaling symmetry yields sparsity, rotation symmetry low rank, and permutation symmetry merged, identical neurons | Ziyin (2024), [LIT-1014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1014.md), read in [NOTE-716](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-716.md). If a per-sample loss is invariant under the reflection I − 2OOᵀ, then Oᵀθ = 0 is a stationary condition for GD and SGD. The Hessian is block diagonal there. Above a critical weight decay all minima satisfy the constraint. Under SGD with strong noise the subspace is attractive even at a strict saddle, by a Lyapunov-exponent argument. Rescaling, rotation and permutation symmetries imply mirrors, so they yield sparsity, low rank and merged neurons, with collapse and loss of plasticity as consequences. Proposed: the SGD half is approximate and the network evidence is limited. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-228](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-228.md) | At the population optimum of the spectral contrastive loss, linear-probe error is bounded by the probability that augmentation changes the label divided by the squared sparsest-partition conductance of the augmentation graph | HaoChen, Wei, Gaidon & Ma (2021), [LIT-249](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-249.md), read in [NOTE-740](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-740.md). On a finite augmentation space, with labels recoverable from augmentations up to error α and k ≥ 2r, every population minimizer of the spectral contrastive loss has linear-probe error Õ(α/ρ²_⌊k/2⌋), where ρ is the sparsest-partition conductance of the augmentation graph (Thm 3.8). The guarantee needs no conditional independence of the views given the label. It is a statement about the population optimum of one loss: it says nothing about what training reaches, nothing about InfoNCE, and its infinite-space extension is asserted, not proved. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-229](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-229.md) | For a symmetrized Barlow Twins loss on a linear or fixed-kernel model, gradient flow from small initialization learns the top eigenvectors of the pairs' symmetrized cross-correlation one at a time, in order of eigenvalue, and ends at the minimum-norm zero-loss solution, kernel PCA | Simon et al. (2023), [LIT-242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-242.md), read in [NOTE-741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-741.md). For L = ‖C − I‖²_F with λ = 1, no batch norm and C symmetrized by hand, a linear model from aligned initialization learns mode j at τ_j ≈ −log(s_j(0)²γ_j)/(8γ_j) (Prop. 4.1, proved), the top spectral solutions are exactly the minimum-norm zero-loss ones (Prop. 4.3), and the kernel version is kernel PCA on K_Γ (Prop. 5.1). Generic small initialization is covered by an informal derivation only. The operator is built from the model's kernel and the sample pairs, not from the positive-pair density ratio, and the stepwise growth seen in ResNets under SimCLR and VICReg is an experiment, not a consequence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-238](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-238.md) v2 | The expected generalization error of an encoder–decoder learner is bounded by the encoder alone, through the KL divergence of its train-and-ghost latents to a prior symmetric under label-preserving permutations, for any decoder, and the bound stays finite for deterministic continuous encoders under lossy compression | Sefidgaran, Zaidi & Krasnowski (2023), [LIT-245](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-245.md), read in [NOTE-742](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-742.md). Theorem 4: E[gen] ≤ inf 2√((2·MDL + K + 2)/n) + ε, where MDL is the expected KL of the joint law of the latents of the training set and an independent ghost set to any prior invariant under label-preserving permutations, and ε is the distortion allowed by lossy compression. It holds for any decoder. With a product prior it reduces to sample-wise mutual information. The bound is never evaluated, the prior may depend on unseen ghost data, and a 2√((K+2)/n) floor remains. It does not prove that I(X;U) cannot bound generalization. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-239](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-239.md) v2 | For any joint law of an input and a context, symmetric or not, the top-d left singular functions of the conditional-expectation operator attain the minimum, over d-dimensional spans, of worst-case linear-probe approximation error over tasks of compatibility at least 1 − ε, namely (s₁² − (1 − ε)²)/(s₁² − s²_{d+1}) when s_{d+1} < 1 − ε ≤ s₁, though other spans can tie | Zhai (2025), [LIT-975](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-975.md), read in [NOTE-770](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-770.md): Lemma 1.4, Theorem 3.2 and Theorem 3.4 with App. B. The operator g ↦ E[g(A)\|X] runs from L²(P_A) to L²(P_X) and is never assumed self-adjoint; its singular value decomposition comes from composing it with its adjoint. The guarantee is for linear probes and approximation error at the population level only. It does not cover a non-reversible kernel on one space, which the thesis never works through, nor what a trained network reaches. | Active |
| [THEORY-241](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-241.md) | Fitting the same function in the same architecture does not fix the internal decomposition: SGD reproduces three Picbreeder images from random weights without the reuse and factoring of the evolved networks, and perturbing its weights breaks the regularities that perturbing the evolved networks' weights preserves | Kumar, Clune, Lehman & Stanley (2025), [LIT-944](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-944.md), read in [NOTE-771](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-771.md). For the skull, butterfly and apple CPPNs, SGD in the layerized evolved architecture fits the image, the network's whole function on the grid. It shows no reuse of the symmetric parts, and single-weight and random-direction sweeps distort the output, where the evolved networks' sweeps vary it meaningfully. Qualitative, curated and three images. The paper's account of why, the order of discovery in open-ended search, and its extension to large models are conjecture. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-244](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-244.md) | Shannon entropy, mutual information and the distortion-rate function are the expectations of their Kolmogorov counterparts only to within the complexity of the source distribution | Grünwald & Vitányi (2004), [LIT-224](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-224.md), read in [NOTE-776](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-776.md). For computable f: 0 ≤ E_f K(x) − H(f) ≤ K(f) + O(1) (Thm 2.10); I(X;Y) − K(f) < E I(x:y) < I(X;Y) + 2K(f) (Thm 3.6). The expected structure function brackets D*_m(R) with a K(f, d, m, R) shift in rate, and equals D*(R) per symbol in the limit (Thm 6.27). Sufficiency links only one way (Thm 5.13). None of this holds for a complex or unknown source, or for one string. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-246](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-246.md) | Training objectives that tighten the class clusters of a classifier's last layers buy accuracy on the trained classes and pay for it in new tasks: among ImageNet-trained ResNet-50s, fixed penultimate features with more class separation transfer worse to datasets with other classes, the difference lies in the last few blocks, and fine-tuning removes it | Kornblith, Chen, Lee & Norouzi (2021), [LIT-1044](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1044.md), read in [NOTE-762](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-762.md). Across nine objectives for ResNet-50 on ImageNet, penultimate class separation R² runs from 0.349 (softmax) to 0.845 (squared error), Papyan's Tr(Σ_W Σ_B†)/C from 21.2 to 0.33, and mean linear transfer to eight new-class datasets falls with R² (Spearman ρ = −0.93), from 75.9% to 48.3%. Cosine-softmax temperature raises R² from 0.24 to 0.77 and lowers transfer from 76.0% to 58.9%. CKA puts the differences in the last third of the network; fine-tuning erases them. The cost is for new classes: relearning the training classes, more separation helps. Networks early-stopped near 92% training accuracy; one dataset; correlational across losses. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-248](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-248.md) v2 | The expected generalisation error of a learning algorithm is at most √(2σ²R/n) + ε, where R is the least information about the sample carried by any surrogate output whose expected generalisation error is within ε; I(S;W) is the lossless case, and for an L-Lipschitz loss R is at most the rate-distortion function of the output's law at distortion ε/(2L), so the bound is finite wherever that function is, including where I(S;W) is infinite | Sefidgaran, Gohari, Richard & Şimşekli (COLT 2022), [LIT-236](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-236.md), read in [NOTE-780](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-780.md). Theorem 4: \|E gen\| ≤ √(2σ²·R_E(ε)/n) + ε, where R_E(ε) is the least I(S;Ŵ) over surrogates within ε in expected generalisation error. For a Lipschitz loss R_E is bounded by the rate-distortion function of P_W (Corollary 6). Theorem 10 is a tail version over a KL ball. The block-coding meaning is proved for finite alphabets only. No bound is evaluated for a learned model, and every bound depends on the unknown data distribution. | Active |
| [THEORY-253](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-253.md) | In a model of independent skills with linear task vectors, sequential onset of acquisition comes from the optimizer: under gradient descent orthogonal skills are learned together at rates set by their frequencies, while under sign descent they compete for coordinate signs, so each starts as the previous finishes | Liu, Liu, Michaud, Gore and Tegmark (2025), [LIT-951](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-951.md), read in [NOTE-794](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-794.md). The Geometry model has loss Σ p_i L((θ − θ₀)·t_i) with orthogonal t_i. In it, SGD learns task 2 in time ∝ 1/p₂, while SignGD holds task 2 back until task 1 is done and then takes a constant extra delay (t₂/t₁ → 2). A rotated quadratic shows the same split (Fig. 12). The order is frequency order either way. The evidence is simulation and one fitted ODE. Sequential onset caused by dependency between skills is a separate experiment, not part of this account. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-259](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-259.md) | Ideal MDL and Bayesian MAP selection under the universal prior agree only to within the complexity of the hypothesis's likelihood, and only among hypotheses for which the data are individually random | Vitányi & Li (1999/2000), [LIT-225](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-225.md), read in [NOTE-801](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-801.md). Theorem 3: if D is Martin-Löf random for Pr(·\|H) and H for the prior P, then −log Pr(D\|H) − log P(H) lies within α = K(Pr(·\|H)) + K(P) below K(D\|H) + K(H). Theorem 4: among such hypotheses, the posteriors of the ideal-MDL and MAP choices differ by at most 2^{−α}. α can be as large as K(H). Outside that set the two can diverge, even on the true hypothesis. "Compression equals Bayes" holds only for typical data and simple hypotheses. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-263](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-263.md) | A coding rate that varies with the realised sample and output makes rate-distortion generalisation bounds data-dependent, and with the rate set to the pointwise information density log dP_{W\|S}/dP(W) against a fixed prior the bound is the disintegrated PAC-Bayes bound | Sefidgaran & Zaidi (2023; IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 2024), [LIT-233](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-233.md), read in [NOTE-806](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-806.md). Theorem 1: with a sample-dependent rate R_{S,W}, gen ≤ √(4σ²(R_{S,W} + log(√(2n)/δ))/(2n−1) + ε). With R_{S,W} = log dP_{W\|S}/dP(W) the coding condition holds at ε = 0 and the bound is the disintegrated PAC-Bayes bound. The general Theorems 3–5 recover Rivasplata et al.'s PAC-Bayes bound and Xu–Raginsky's. The coding construction is proved for finite alphabets only. The general proofs are change of measure. The rate is a Shannon code-length difference against a prior, not Kolmogorov complexity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-266.md) | The average generalisation error along an optimisation trajectory is bounded by the rate-distortion function of the trajectory's law given the sample, plus a coupling term that carries the trajectory's dependence on the sample | Sefidgaran & Zaidi (2023), [LIT-233](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-233.md), Theorem 7, read in [NOTE-806](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-806.md). For an L-Lipschitz loss in [0, 1], with probability ≥ 1 − δ, the mean of gen(S, W^t) over iterations is at most √((RD(S, ε; π_S) + log(√(2n)M/δ))/(2n − 1) + 4Lε). RD is computed for the sample at hand. The coupling coefficient M depends on the unknown distribution and absorbs I(W^T; S). The CIFAR-10 experiment drops M and 4Lε and shows only that the estimated rate and the test gap fall together over learning rates. For FCN4 the plotted rate term is about 3, which is vacuous for 0–1 loss. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-270](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-270.md) | Translation without parallel data is learnable from a plausibility prior over the target language alone, with error falling in the common ground between prior and translations, in the size of the source language and in the number of samples | Goldwasser, Gruber, Kalai and Paradise (NeurIPS 2023), [LIT-941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-941.md), read in [NOTE-804](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-804.md). Proved for maximum likelihood in stylised random models with uniform languages and one-to-one translators; in one model the bound O(log\|Θ\| / (α·min(m,\|T\|))) is tight up to a constant. Information- theoretic only. The prior substitutes for parallel data in learning the decoder, not for information in a message. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-274](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-274.md) | Sequence models trained only on a graph's edge bigrams store it as a global embedding geometry, not as a lookup, although the lookup is expressible, found faster and no less succinct; in a wide two-layer weight-tied model the geometry is the top Laplacian eigenspace, reached by cross-entropy training without a rank bottleneck, regularization or multi-hop supervision | Noroozizadeh, Nagarajan, Rosenfeld & Kumar (2025), [LIT-995](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-995.md), read in [NOTE-800](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-800.md). Empirical throughout: path-star graphs up to 5×10⁴ nodes, four tiny graphs, frozen-embedding controls; the two-layer spectral analysis is informal and rests on an unproved observation (App. F). It does not explain why deeper models prefer the geometry, which the paper poses as open, and its main transformer runs used weight decay. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-277.md) | For individual data, at every bound on model complexity, the model with the shortest two-part code is, to within O(log n), the best-fitting model in randomness deficiency, although the fit itself cannot be computed or approximated | Vereshchagin & Vitányi (2002/2004), [LIT-239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-239.md), read in [NOTE-787](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-787.md), Theorem IV.8: β_x(α) + K(x) and λ_x(α) agree to within O(log n) for a string of length n. Every set minimising K(S) + log \|S\| at complexity α is within O(log n) of the best fit there. h_x and λ_x are upper semicomputable, while β_x is not semicomputable. Restated by Grünwald & Vitányi, [LIT-224](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-224.md), §6.2. Finite-set models; computable distributions at O(log n) cost. It says nothing at the (k/2) log n scale of parametric model selection, and nothing about K(A) + K(x \| A). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-278.md) | Under MSE loss a trained classifier stays near the least-squares classifier for its own features, and on that central path, for unconstrained features continually renormalized to identity within-class covariance, gradient flow drives the class-separation singular values to infinity at equal rates, which is neural collapse | Han, Papyan & Donoho (2021), [LIT-974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-974.md), read in [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md). MSE loss splits exactly into a least-squares term and a non-negative deviation term, and the deviation becomes negligible early in training in 15 dataset–network cells. On that central path, with λ = 0, the loss is ½ Σ 1/(ω_j² + C) in the singular values of Σ_W^(−1/2)M̃. Under a flow that re-whitens the features after every step, each ω_j grows as (4t/N)^(1/4), and their ratios tend to 1. That is NC1 and NC2, and NC3–NC4 follow. Not shown: that ordinary training is this flow, or anything for cross-entropy or with weight decay. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-279](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-279.md) | Early in training, image classifiers and language models act on the low-order statistics of their inputs, first-order before second-order, and later lose that sensitivity as they come to use higher-order structure | Belrose et al. (2024, ICML), [LIT-952](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-952.md), read in [NOTE-777](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-777.md). Over training, ConvNeXt V2, Swin V2 and RegNet-Y on five small image datasets are probed with images whose class means or covariances are grafted from another class, and with maximum-entropy samples that keep only those statistics. Accuracy on these rises and then falls, often below chance. Pythia fits unigram-sampled text before bigram-sampled text. The ordering is empirical and covers orders one and two. The Taylor argument that motivates it is a heuristic, and the paper does not measure an ordered sequence beyond second order. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-283](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-283.md) v2 | For a hierarchical multi-index target with isotropic Gaussian inputs and even, separable links, direction k becomes weakly recoverable by the Bayes-optimal estimator at a sample count proportional to its squared weight to the power minus one, so features emerge one at a time through sharp spectral transitions in the number of samples; a target-agnostic spectral estimator attains the thresholds and the optimal weighted error, and a two-layer network whose first layer is that estimator, with a ridge readout, attains them in excess risk | Defilippis, Krzakala, Loureiro and Maillard (2026), [LIT-940](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-940.md), read in [NOTE-805](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-805.md). Take x ~ N(0, I/d), n = αd, and f⋆ = Σ a_k g_k(⟨w_k, x⟩) with even links of generative exponent two and a_k ~ k^(−γ). Direction k is weakly recoverable at α_k = Θ(a_k^(−2)) (Thm. 3.2). The optimal weighted error is Θ(α^(−1+1/(2γ))) until α ≍ m⋆^(2γ). The spectral estimator on Σ T(y_i)x_ix_iᵀ attains both (Thm. 3.6). The cascade is in the number of samples, not in training time. The network result is for a spectral first layer plus a ridge readout, not gradient descent. | Active |
| [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md) v2 | Under class imbalance the last-layer geometry that unregularized cross-entropy prefers is not the simplex ETF but simplex-encoded-label interpolation: the logits equal the simplex-encoded labels, the classifier and embedding Gram matrices come from that matrix's SVD, any finite weight decay changes the geometry, and training approaches it more slowly as imbalance grows | Thrampoulidis et al. (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md). For the unconstrained-features max-margin problem under STEP imbalance, every solution has logits ŴᵀĤ = Ẑ (one-hot minus 1/k), ĤᵀĤ = UΛUᵀ and ŴᵀŴ = VΛVᵀ from Ẑ's SVD (Theorem 1). This is the ETF only if the data are balanced or binary. No finite ridge gives it under imbalance (Proposition 1), though the ridge path tends to it (Proposition 2). ResNet-18 and VGG-13 runs sit closer to SELI than to the ETF, and approach it more slowly at larger R. Not shown: that gradient descent reaches it, and anything with more than one seed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-289](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-289.md) | When each round of a fixed-design linear regression is refit to labels generated by the previous fit, keeping every earlier round's data bounds the test error at π²/6 times the first fit's, where replacing the data makes it grow linearly in the number of rounds | Gerstgrasser, Schaeffer, Dey et al. (2024), [LIT-971](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-971.md), read in [NOTE-815](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-815.md), Theorems 1–2 extending Dohmatob et al.'s replace result. Proved for ridgeless OLS with isotropic Gaussian features, the real covariates reused every round and only labels regenerated. The error is bounded, not constant: it rises every round towards its limit, and every model remains a noisier copy of the first. Small language and diffusion models behave alike over five to eight rounds; a VAE's error still rises. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-293](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-293.md) | For an optimal capacity-bounded learner on a mixture of equally frequent random facts and a second domain, the facts are learned not at all below a capacity threshold set by the mixing ratio and in full above it, and Pythia models trained on such mixtures show the same threshold in model size and in mixing ratio | Gu, Lyu, Li and Zhang (2025), [LIT-984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-984.md), read in [NOTE-796](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-796.md). Proved for an idealised learner whose capacity is mutual information with the data (Theorem 4.3), on an orthogonal mixture of uniform facts and a second domain; seen in Pythia models from 14M to 6.9B on synthetic biographies mixed into web text. The theory is static. It does not say when in training the facts arrive, and it does not show that SGD reaches the optimal allocation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-294.md) | Lazy-regime training of a wide shallow network does not collapse its features: on two-class Gaussian data the expected within-class variability of the NTK features is that of the NNGP features at initialization | Kothapalli & Tirer (2024), [LIT-985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-985.md), read in [NOTE-774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-774.md). NC1 = tr Σ_W / tr Σ_B of kernel-defined features is a closed function of the kernel matrix (Theorem 4.1). For one-dimensional data, two classes on opposite sides of the origin and zero bias, the ReLU NTK of a wide two-layer net is a within-class rescaling of the NNGP kernel. So the expected NC1 is the same (Theorem 5.1). In higher dimensions it is measured no lower, and for ReLU higher. A narrow theorem with a suggestive generalization. The inference that collapse requires feature learning is the reading's, not proved. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-314](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-314.md) v2 | Every minimizer of an arbitrary cost on the training outputs plus a strictly increasing function of the RKHS norm lies in the span of the kernel functions at the training points, by the reproducing property and orthogonal decomposition alone | Schölkopf, Herbrich & Smola (2001), [LIT-261](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-261.md), Theorem 1 with its proof (eqs. 18–24), read in [NOTE-836](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-836.md) and checked. No convexity of the cost and no Riesz theorem is used; the RKHS is built from the kernel, so the reproducing property holds by construction. The theorem is stated over countable kernel expansions of finite norm, assumes a minimizer exists, and does not cover costs that see f other than through its values at the training points. | Active |
| [THEORY-318](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-318.md) | A bound on the max-information between a dataset and the functions an analyst chooses bounds the probability that an adaptively chosen statistic overfits that dataset, and differential privacy supplies the bound, so a holdout can validate many adaptively chosen statistics | Dwork, Feldman, Hardt, Pitassi, Reingold & Roth (2015), [LIT-964](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-964.md), Supplementary Material only, read in [NOTE-848](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-848.md) (Skimmed: the main text was not reached). Theorem 2 and Lemma 5 are proved there and were checked: P[overfit] ≤ 2^{I∞}·max P[overfit], and ε-DP gives I∞ ≤ log₂e·εn. Thresholdout's guarantee (Theorem 11), n = O(ln(m/β)/τ²·min{B, √(B ln(m/β))/τ}), is stated with its proof elsewhere. Statistical queries on a discrete universe only, and a procedure that prevents inflation, not a correction for a search already run. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-319](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-319.md) | When two views are redundant for a label, the predictor that infers one view from the other is within εX + 2√(εXεZ) + εZ of the Bayes predictor, and it is linear in the contrastive density ratio, so a linear readout of m random evaluations of that ratio approaches it at rate 1/m, with no symmetry between the views required | Tosh, Krishnamurthy & Hsu (2021), [LIT-251](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-251.md), read in [NOTE-841](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-841.md): Lemma 1, §2.3–2.4, Lemma 2 and Theorem 3. The label enters only through how redundant the views are about it; the representation is the density ratio p(x,z)/(p(x)p(z)), learned without labels. Population level. The error-propagation results need a uniform bound on the ratio, and the low-dimensional direct embeddings are shown to exist, not to be reached. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-320](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-320.md) v2 | In a spectral contrastive graph that joins labelled known classes to unlabelled data, a novel labelling's linear-probe residual is exactly its part outside the top eigenspace that the labelled rows of the discarded eigenvectors cannot absorb, so which partition of the unlabelled data is discovered depends on the known classes: ones sharing the target's attribute can remove the residual, and ones sharing a rival attribute can raise it | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li (2023), [LIT-235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-235.md), read in [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md). On the population graph, at the exact rank-k optimum, R(U*, y) = ‖(I − P_{L♭})U♭ᵀy‖² (Theorem 5.5, stated as ≤, proved as = in C.1). In a one-sample-per-kind toy, a known class sharing colour makes a colour labelling recoverable, and one sharing shape makes it worse than none (Lemma 5.4). The general error bound (Theorem 5.6) is approximate and pools all known classes into one block, and is not part of this account. Nothing here is about trained networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-331](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-331.md) | Counting the inference a model will serve as well as its training, the least-compute way to reach a fixed quality shifts toward up-front compute as expected inference volume grows: a smaller model trained on more data in Sardana et al., a larger pretrained model over test-time search in Snell et al.; test-time compute won only at low volume and on questions the small model already sometimes solved | Sardana et al. (2024; arXiv 2023), [LIT-1070](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1070.md), read in [NOTE-881](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-881.md), and Snell et al. (2024), [LIT-1063](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1063.md), read in [NOTE-869](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-869.md). Sardana et al. minimise training plus lifetime inference FLOPs at a fixed loss under a Chinchilla-fitted law: the optimum moves to smaller models trained longer as known demand grows (28% fewer FLOPs at 30B quality and 10^13 inference tokens), and 47 runs show loss still falling at extreme ratios but more slowly than the law predicts. Snell et al. match FLOPs between a small model with test-time search or revision and a ~14× larger model on MATH: test-time compute wins at a low ratio of inference to pretraining tokens on easier questions and loses at a high ratio, and on the hardest at every ratio. Both take expected use as a known aggregate; neither has staleness or uncertainty about demand, and Snell's evidence is one model family on 500 questions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-342](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-342.md) | In AlphaZero on 9×9 Hex, at fixed playing strength, training compute and tree-search compute substitute along a straight line in log–log space, about 15× less search for each 10× more training over about two decades of training compute, down to a one-node search; the trade is measured for one search and counts no games played | Jones (2021), [LIT-1069](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1069.md), read in [NOTE-884](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-884.md). Across about 200 AlphaZero models on Hex boards 3×3 to 9×9, the best Elo for a given training compute follows one change-point curve, shifted by a fixed factor of compute per board row. On 9×9 only, iso-Elo contours of training against test-time search compute are straight in log–log space (fit: log test = −1.2·log train + 0.004·Elo + 29) over roughly 1e14–1e16 FLOPS-seconds of training, ending at a one-node search. One game, one nonstandard implementation, no uncertainty on the fitted coefficients, and no count of how many searches the trained agent will run, so it gives an exchange rate, not an amortization. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-349](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-349.md) | For binary outcomes and a fixed representation of individuals, a predictor can pass every test in a bounded class without being close to nature: outcome indistinguishability to tests that see the sampled prediction is equivalent, with stated losses, to multicalibration over a closely related class of sets, a predictor meeting it exists at size polynomial in the tests' size and the tolerance whatever nature's complexity, and learning one is as hard as weak agnostic learning of the class | Dwork, Kim, Reingold, Rothblum and Yona (2021), [LIT-1068](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1068.md), read in [NOTE-885](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-885.md), and Hébert-Johnson, Kim, Reingold and Rothblum (2018), [LIT-1052](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1052.md), read in [NOTE-879](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-879.md). A predictor is outcome indistinguishable relative to a class of distinguishers when none can tell nature's outcomes from outcomes drawn from the predictor, up to ε. With no access or sample access to the predictor this is equivalent to multi-accuracy or multicalibration over closely related classes, and a predictor meeting it exists at size O(s/ε²) (O(s/α⁴γ) for multicalibration), independent of nature. Learning a multicalibrated predictor is equivalent to weak agnostic learning of the class. Adequacy here is relative to the class, the outcome and the features, and is not unique; it is not closeness to the truth, and the papers say nothing about signal detection. | Active |
| [THEORY-354](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-354.md) | An observer's power to refute a predictor depends on its access to the predictor as well as on its budget: against tests that see only the sampled prediction a predictor of size O(s/ε²) always passes, but if fine-grained clique counting is hard, or BPP ≠ PSPACE, some cheap tests that may query the predictor adaptively pass only predictors about as costly as nature's own | Dwork, Kim, Reingold, Rothblum and Yona (2021), [LIT-1068](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1068.md), read in [NOTE-885](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-885.md). Against sample-access distinguishers of size s an outcome-indistinguishable predictor of size O(s/ε²) always exists. Against oracle-access distinguishers, under fine-grained hardness of clique counting or BPP ≠ PSPACE, there are natures and polynomially many cheap distinguishers such that no predictor much cheaper than nature is indistinguishable. Non-adaptive queries add little; the power comes from adaptive queries. The results are conditional and asymptotic, with upper and lower bounds in different parameterisations; they say nothing about human observers or about which access a real auditor has. | Active |
| [THEORY-359](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-359.md) | Cognitive mechanisms can be derived as the one, among those a brain can execute, that best trades the expected utility of its result against the opportunity cost of the time and resources it uses; the review shows the derivation reproducing many heuristics and biases, not that people are optimal, and the objective is per episode | Lieder & Griffiths (2020; online 2019), [LIT-1071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1071.md), read in [NOTE-873](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-873.md). Resource rationality picks the heuristic that maximizes expected utility of its result minus the expected opportunity cost of the time and resources it uses (Eq. 3), averaged over environments consistent with what is known (Eq. 4), and a five-step method derives process models from it. The support is a review of others' models recast in this frame, with numbers from those studies. The authors offer optimality as a methodological device, not a claim about people, and the method lets constraints be refitted to data. The objective is per episode, with no terms for storing, retrieving or reusing a result, or for its going stale. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-439](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-439.md) | Given the same few demonstrations, temporarily updating a language model's weights on them and then conditioning beats conditioning alone, most on tasks with structural rules or distribution shift and most when the update is trained in the in-context format: for models of 1–8B parameters, examples used as context and the same examples used as a training signal are not interchangeable | Akyürek et al. (2024; ICML 2025), [LIT-796](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-796.md), read in [NOTE-637](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-637.md). On BIG-Bench Hard with Llama 3.1 8B and 10 demonstrations over five seeds, zero-shot 40.9%, in-context 50.5%, per-task LoRA test-time training then in-context 57.8%; 12 of 27 tasks gain at least 2 points, and Boolean expressions falls. Training the update on leave-one-out in-context tasks beats training on bare pairs (57.8% against 51.5%). The update is discarded after each task, so it is as transient as a context. It is two benchmarks and one model family, and which task property predicts the gain is open. | Active |
| [THEORY-481](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-481.md) v2 | A linear-attention layer trained on in-context regression learns as a two-layer linear network does: when tasks share the input covariance's eigenbasis and the weights stay aligned with it, then in the long-context limit each input mode is learned on its own logistic curve whose timescale falls with the square of its variance, so learning is staged by the input spectrum, and the layer converges to a preconditioned estimator; at finite context length the modes decouple exactly only when inputs are isotropic, and otherwise couple at order 1/N | Mainali & Teixeira (2025), [LIT-859](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-859.md), read in [NOTE-658](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-658.md). The prediction of one linear-attention layer reduces to p₂ W Σ̂_x q₁ x_q, a product of two learned factors, so averaged gradient flow decouples into modes with τ_α dp_α/dt = q_α(1 − p_α q_α s^∞_α) and τ_α = (ηP s_α²)⁻¹, logistic from a balanced start. The fixed point ŷ = W Σ̂_x [((N+1)/N)Σ_x + (Tr Σ_x/N)I]⁻¹ x_q is the one Ahn et al. and Zhang, Frei & Bartlett found; the trajectory is new. The decoupling into independent modes is exact as N → ∞. At finite N it holds only for isotropic inputs with equal modes: the paper commutes the non-diagonal empirical covariance at (A71) and (A73), and the correct Wishart moment couples the modes at order 1/N. Alignment of the weights with the data's eigenbasis is assumed throughout, the null blocks vanish only in expectation over tasks, and the transfer to non-linear transformers is timing coincidences. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-510](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-510.md) | How much of an ImageNet image a crop must keep for its label to survive varies widely by class, with architectures agreeing on which classes are fragile, and strengthening random crop raises mean accuracy while some classes lose 20 points or more; how many classes lose is not established | Balestriero, Bottou & LeCun (2022), [LIT-234](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-234.md), read in [NOTE-845](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-845.md). Six pretrained models on cropped test images keep some classes recognisable at an 8% crop and lose others below about 50%, and agree on which. Over 20 ResNet-50 runs, moving the crop lower bound from 100% to 8% raises mean accuracy from about 70% to 76% while "academic gown" falls from about 62% to 40%. The classes shown are hand-picked; the per-class test rejects for 4.4% of classes at the 5% level, uncorrected for 1,000 tests, which alone is not more than chance; and evaluation-set noise is not counted. Theorem 1 does not reach which classes pay. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-521](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-521.md) | In the thermodynamic limit, with examples and capacity growing together at fixed load, generalization error can jump discontinuously with the load when the entropy of hypotheses just above the best error vanishes faster than the training-error energy grows: a spherical perceptron's error falls smoothly as 1/α, an Ising perceptron's drops to zero at a critical load | Martin & Mahoney (2017), [LIT-672](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-672.md), read in [NOTE-542](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-542.md), restating Seung, Sompolinsky & Tishby (1992) and Haussler, Kearns, Seung & Tishby (1996), which the record does not hold. Generalization is set by maximizing s(ε) − α ln(1/(1 − ε)). For weights on a sphere s(ε) ~ ln ε and ε ~ 1/α; for ±1 weights s(ε) ~ −(π²/2)ε² ln ε, the first-order condition has no solution past a critical load, and the error drops to zero. Uniform bounds that see a class only through its size or VC dimension are smooth and blind to this. That deep networks have such a phase diagram is the authors' conjecture, and their mapping of label noise to load and early stopping to temperature is an analogy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-574](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-574.md) | The structural width of Xin Li's learning programme is a covering number of the margin-safe region by local pieces: its lower bounds come from metric confinement through a wedge point, not from topology, labels enter only through the margin, and the error floor below width binds only learners assembled from local experts, so it does not entail routing, nor training routing apart from the task loss | Li (2026), [LIT-376](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md) (Local Urysohn Width, v1), [LIT-375](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-375.md) (Structural Learning Theory) and [LIT-374](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md) (Structural Decoupling), read jointly in [NOTE-323](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-323.md), [NOTE-324](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-324.md) and [NOTE-322](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-322.md). In repaired form the formal core holds: width is incomparable with the per-cell VC dimension, fewer cells than width give an error floor (under an assumption that states it), and discovering all basins costs Ω(w log w) samples. But local correctness is automatic on any connected patch, the bouquet lower bound is metric (the paper's Remark 8.11 concedes it), a global classifier has width 1 (Remark 3.4), and the additive Rademacher bound said to call for decoupled training holds for joint training too. | Active |
| [THEORY-614](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-614.md) v2 | If pretraining text is a mixture of hidden Markov models indexed by a latent concept and a model fits that distribution exactly, then a prompt of concatenated examples moves the posterior onto the prompt's concept, and the in-context predictor becomes Bayes-optimal as examples accumulate, whenever each example's evidence for the concept outweighs the cost of the improbable transitions between examples; whether trained networks learn in context this way is not shown | Xie, Raghunathan, Liang & Ma (2021), [LIT-797](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-797.md), read in [NOTE-633](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-633.md). Theorem 1 is proved under Assumptions 1–5 and a distinguishability condition; Theorems 2–3 give roughly 1/k excess risk without it. The proofs were not followed in the reading. [NOTE-633](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-633.md) declined a THEORY because the result is conditional on exact fit to a specific generative model, so it is a consequence of that model, not a fact about language models. It is filed Proposed under the owner's ruling, with the condition in the title. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-726](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-726.md) | Weight decay on factors is a nuclear-norm penalty on their product: with tied weights λ‖W‖²_F = λ‖WWᵀ‖_*, and for untied factors the least (‖U‖²_F + ‖V‖²_F)/2 over UVᵀ = M is ‖M‖_*, so for any loss that sees the weights only through the product, square-penalized training is nuclear-norm-penalized training of a product of bounded rank | Boncoraglio et al. (2025), [LIT-857](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-857.md), Appendix A, read in [NOTE-661](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-661.md), and re-derived here. ‖W‖²_F = Tr(WWᵀ) = ‖WWᵀ‖_*, since a PSD matrix's singular values are its eigenvalues. For untied factors, Hölder's inequality for Schatten norms and AM–GM bound ‖M‖_* by (‖U‖²_F + ‖V‖²_F)/2 over every factorization UVᵀ = M, and the balanced SVD factorization attains it. The product's rank is bounded by the factors' inner dimension. It says nothing about what the trained product looks like, which is [THEORY-180](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-180.md)'s spectral law. | Active |
| [THEORY-735](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-735.md) | Under a local quadratic model of the loss with the greedy optimal step, per-step progress at batch size B is ΔL_max/(1 + B_noise/B), and at fixed B the steps and examples needed satisfy (S/S_min − 1)(E/E_min − 1) = 1, with E_min/S_min the progress-weighted mean of B_noise | McCandlish, Kaplan, Amodei et al. (2018), [LIT-348](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-348.md), §2 and App. D.1, as read and re-derived in [NOTE-293](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-293.md). A derivation under stated assumptions: a second-order model of the loss along the step, an unbiased minibatch gradient of covariance Σ/B, and the step size that maximises the expected decrease. It says nothing about whether real training meets those assumptions, or how well the noise scale predicts the measured critical batch, which is [THEORY-033](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-033.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-737](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-737.md) | In a spectral contrastive graph that joins labelled known classes to unlabelled data, the least-squares residual of a novel labelling on the top-k eigenspace, with the labelled entries left free, equals exactly the part of the labelling outside that eigenspace that the labelled rows of the discarded eigenvectors cannot absorb | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li (2023), [LIT-235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-235.md), Theorem 5.5 with its proof in C.1, read in [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md). The paper states the identity as ≤, and its proof is a chain of equalities. Re-derived here in three steps from orthogonality and least squares. With the paper's Lemma 5.1 it bounds the novel labelling's 0–1 linear-probe error by twice this residual. It is about the exact rank-k factorization of a population graph, not about trained networks. | Active |
| [THEORY-738](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-738.md) | In the unconstrained-features max-margin problem with k classes under step imbalance and feature dimension at least k − 1, the unique optimal logits are the simplex-encoded labels, every margin equals one, and the classifier and embedding Gram matrices are the two square-root factors of that matrix's singular value decomposition; the geometry is the simplex equiangular tight frame exactly when the classes are balanced or there are two of them | Thrampoulidis, Kini, Vakilian and Behnia (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), Theorem 1 and Corollary 1.3, read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md) and re-derived here. By [THEORY-726](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-726.md) the problem is nuclear-norm minimisation of the logits under margin constraints. The polar factor of the simplex-encoded label matrix certifies it optimal, because under step imbalance its off-diagonal entries are negative. It does not say that gradient descent or trained networks reach this geometry, which is [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-739](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-739.md) | For the quartic proxy of word2vec with tied weights, symmetric reweighting and constant weights, the rank-d minimisers are the top d eigenvectors of the relative deviation-from-independence matrix M*, scaled by the square roots of their eigenvalues, up to rotation; and from an initialisation aligned with those eigenvectors, gradient flow acquires each one in an independent logistic rise, in order of eigenvalue | Karkada, Simon, Bahri and DeWeese (2025), [LIT-855](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-855.md), Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, read in [NOTE-660](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-660.md) and re-derived here. The quartic proxy is a function of WWᵀ alone, so von Neumann's trace inequality gives its rank-d minimisers. Gradient flow from an aligned start keeps the eigenbasis and reduces each mode to a logistic equation. It does not say that word2vec, or the proxy from random initialisation, behaves this way; that is [THEORY-182](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-182.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-740](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-740.md) | A two-layer linear network trained by gradient flow on white inputs from a decoupled, balanced start learns each singular mode of its input–output correlation in a logistic rise that waits a time of order its inverse strength times the log of the inverse initial scale, so the modes arrive one at a time in order of strength; a single-layer network on the same data learns every mode on one timescale with no plateau, so under these conditions the stages come from the product of layers and the data's spectrum | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2014, 2019), [LIT-864](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-864.md) and [LIT-862](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-862.md), read in [NOTE-667](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-667.md) and [NOTE-666](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-666.md), re-derived here. From a decoupled, balanced start the two-layer equations keep the SVD basis of Σyx, and each mode's strength obeys τȧ = 2a(s − a), a logistic rise. One weight matrix on the same data relaxes every mode exponentially on the one timescale τ. It does not say that random starts follow the solution, which is [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md)'s. | Active |
